title: Body size predicts how long ant workers live - but not how they age or how they die from heat
abstract: arXiv:2608.14245v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: In social insects, mortality risk comprises distinct components that may not share the same predictors: lifespan duration, senescence trajectory, and thermal vulnerability. We tested these three axes in 18 Australian ant species using paired field-laboratory survival assays (2,363 cohort-day observations; 1,148 workers). Body size predicted duration (Cox HR = 0.67, p = 0.002), while colony size (p = 0.60) and the size x temperature interaction (p = 0.72) showed no detectable moderating effect. A weak but significant size x foraging-rate interaction was detected (LRT p = 0.014), suggesting that intrinsic physiology remains the most parsimonious explanation for the main size-longevity pattern, although ecological context may contribute. Senescence trajectory was associated with circadian niche rather than size: it was steepest in matinal species (Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.009; matinal vs. crepuscular p = 0.002) and was uncorrelated with body

translated_title: 体型大小预测蚂蚁工蚁的寿命——但不预测其衰老方式或因热死亡的方式
translated_abstract: 在社昆虫中，死亡风险包含不同的组成部分，这些部分可能不具有相同的预测因子：寿命长度、衰老轨迹和热脆弱性。我们通过配对野外-实验室生存试验（2,363个群体日观测；1,148只工蚁）测试了18种澳大利亚蚂蚁的这些三个轴。体型大小预测了寿命长度（Cox风险比=0.67，p=0.002），而群体大小（p=0.60）和体型×温度交互作用（p=0.72）没有检测到显著的调节效应。检测到弱但显著的体型×觅食率交互作用（似然比检验p=0.014），表明内在生理学仍然是体型-寿命模式最简洁的解释，尽管生态背景可能有所贡献。衰老轨迹与昼夜节律生态位相关，而非体型：在清晨活动物种中最陡峭（Kruskal-Wallis p=0.009；清晨活动与黄昏活动相比p=0.002），且与体型大小无关。
tldr: 本研究发现蚂蚁工蚁的寿命由体型大小预测，但衰老速度和热死亡脆弱性由昼夜节律生态位决定，而非体型。
en_tdlr: This study finds that ant worker lifespan is predicted by body size, but senescence rate and heat mortality vulnerability are determined by circadian niche, not body size.
